content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem now: the root cause was the monthly-spend-feature flag enabling at 09:02, which exposed a latent divide-by-zero in spend_summary.py on account page renders. The flag revert didn't stick—logs show it flipped back on at 09:10:30—so the error rate stayed elevated until a fix PR was opened and the incident escalated.

I need to be careful with wording constraints: I shouldn't restate given figures as if I'd computed them or invent new numbers, and I should treat the recorded duration as a lower bound since the service hadn't recovered by the end of available metrics. I'll describe impact qualitatively—things like "a substantial minority of account page requests failed" and "errors rose many times above baseline"—rather than citing specific percentages, and I'll flag key assumptions: that the flag-revert failure is inferred from logs rather than a change-management record, that no deploy occurred in this window, that the ClientDisconnected baseline errors are unrelated background noise, and that the service was still broken at handoff. Now I'll write the full postmortem with these constraints in mind.

assumptions: Impact is bounded, not measured: the service was still failing at the end of the metrics read, so the stated duration and error figures are lower bounds. No independent confirmation of recovery exists.

The causal link between the flag turning on and the failures rests on temporal correlation in the logs (a new error signature appearing in the exact minute evaluations flipped to 'on') plus the absence of any recorded deploy, traffic, latency or memory change — not on a reproduction of the fault.

The conclusion that the flag revert failed to propagate is inferred from logs continuing to print the feature as 'on' after the revert, and from a change-log entry showing it on again at 09:10:30. Whether that re-enable was an external actor, a provider default, or the revert simply never reaching the evaluation layer was not established.

The defect is assumed to be latent code shipped in an earlier release: no deployment was found in the windows queried (24 hours, and wider lookbacks of roughly 2 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and 1 month). Absence in the change feed is treated as absence of a deploy.
The low-level 'ClientDisconnected' errors present before 09:02 are treated as ordinary background noise unrelated to this incident.
Scope is assumed limited to the account page because that is the only surface named in the logs read; other endpoints were not examined.
The proposed fix in the draft pull request has not been reviewed, tested or verified to resolve the fault.
input.executive_summary:
Starting at 09:02 UTC on 24 September 2026, a large share of requests to the customer account page in the online shop began failing outright. Shoppers trying to view their account would have seen errors instead of the page; browsing, search and checkout paths are not implicated by the evidence. The trigger was a configuration switch that turned on a new monthly-spend feature; the code behind that feature contains a fault that causes the account page to fail whenever it runs.

Automated response picked the incident up within five minutes of onset, identified the configuration switch as the cause, and turned it back off. That attempt did not work — the service continued to report the feature as active and kept failing — and the switch was recorded as being turned on again shortly afterwards. With no further action available that could address a fault in the code itself, the automation opened a draft code fix for human review and escalated.

The service had not recovered by the last minute of data available, so the outage window and every impact figure attached to it are lower bounds rather than final measurements; the true duration and customer impact are at least as large as reported and remain open until an engineer confirms recovery. Immediate next steps for the on-call team: force the feature off in a way that demonstrably reaches running instances (and confirm from logs that evaluations flip to "off"), then review and land the code fix for the divide-by-zero in the spend-summary path.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` flipped from off to on at 09:02 (no deploy is recorded in the preceding 24 hours, or in the wider windows subsequently queried), which began routing account-page renders through a latent defect at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:35 that raises ZeroDivisionError. Errors appear in exactly the minutes the flag evaluates "on" and carry a signature never seen before that minute. The automated flag revert at 09:07:26 did not take effect — every log minute afterwards still reports the flag evaluating "on" and the ZeroDivisionError continues, and the change log records the flag being switched back on at 09:10:30 — so the underlying defect remained live and the incident was escalated with a draft pull request rather than mitigated.
